# TravelMate-R: Solver-Certified, Weather-Robust Itinerary Planning with LLM Agents

*Draft. Every number in Section 5 is generated by `python -m research.report` into
`research/results/report.md`; the headline figures below are copied from that file.*

## Abstract

LLM travel planners still break hard constraints, and travel-planning benchmarks assume the world is
deterministic: the weather on day three is known when the plan is made. We present TravelMate-R, a
multi-agent planner in which the LLM handles language and preference ranking only. A logic-based
Benders decomposition builds the days: a MILP master assigns places to days, and an exact,
minute-by-minute day verifier returns no-good cuts until every day is feasible, which certifies
optimality. We make the objective weather-aware: each day carries a climatological wet-day
probability (10 years of Open-Meteo rainfall, IMD 2.5 mm rule), the master maximises expected
utility, and it jointly reserves an indoor Plan B for every likely-wet outdoor day. Plans are scored by
a port of TravelPlanner's constraint evaluator (Xie et al., 2024), which also back-prompts LLM
planners in an LLM-Modulo baseline. Results on 40 real Indian trips under two weather regimes
(Nov–Dec and July monsoon) are reported in Section 5.

## 1. Introduction

TravelPlanner showed that strong LLM agents deliver final plans that satisfy every constraint in under
1% of cases. Two families of fixes followed. LLM-Modulo frameworks keep the LLM as a generator and add
external critics that back-prompt it (Kambhampati et al., 2024; Gundawar et al., 2024). Formal
approaches translate the request into SMT or MILP and solve it exactly (Hao et al., 2024; Ju et al.,
2024). Both families evaluate in a static world.

Real trips are not static. For the July versions of our 40 trips, the climatological chance that a
given day is rainy averages 42% (against 7% on the original Nov–Dec dates), so a plan that is optimal
for a dry world can lose value to rained-out outdoor stops. We ask: can an agentic planner give hard
guarantees on schedule feasibility *and* plan for uncertainty it can quantify from open data?

**Contributions.**
1. **Solver-grounded day planning.** A logic-based Benders decomposition (Hooker & Ottosson, 2003)
   over a team-orienteering-with-time-windows model. Its subproblem is the same day simulator the
   production system uses (opening hours, lunch, daily driving budget, day window), so the
   certificate covers the rules a traveller actually sees.
2. **A critic bank ported from TravelPlanner.** We keep TravelPlanner's structure, return
   convention and aggregate metrics (Delivery, Commonsense/Hard Micro/Macro, Final Pass), and map
   its constraints to day trips (10 constraints, Table A1). The same critics back-prompt LLMs in an
   LLM-Modulo baseline.
3. **Weather-robust planning.** We estimate a climatological wet-day probability per day, maximise
   expected utility, and reserve an indoor Plan B per wet outdoor day *inside* the master problem (a
   first-stage reservation, as in two-stage stochastic programming). A new hard constraint, Weather
   Safety, makes the property testable.
4. **A stateless, browser-first deployment.** The planner runs with no database. Reference data
   ships as CSV, caches are in memory, and saved plans live in the user's browser.

## 2. Related work

- **Benchmarks.** TravelPlanner (Xie et al., ICML 2024); its constraint evaluator is the basis of our
  critic bank (`app/planning/critics.py`; MIT licence, attribution in the file header).
- **LLM-Modulo.** Kambhampati et al. (ICML 2024) argue that LLMs are approximate knowledge sources
  that need sound external verifiers; Gundawar et al. (2024) report large TravelPlanner gains from
  critic back-prompting. Our `llm_modulo` baseline reproduces this loop with our critics.
- **Formal planning with LLMs.** Hao et al. (NAACL 2025) translate requests into SMT and use the
  solver's unsat core to drive repair; TTG (Ju et al., 2024) uses MILP with guaranteed-optimal
  output. We follow the "LLM proposes, solver disposes" split, and add stochastic weather, which
  none of these model.
- **Orienteering.** Our master is a team orienteering problem with time windows (Vansteenwegen et
  al., 2011), solved by logic-based Benders decomposition with HiGHS (Huangfu & Hall, 2018).

## 3. System

```
request → Supervisor (LLM: extract) → Geo → ┬ Research (OSM + LLM rank IDs) ┐
                                            ├ Weather (forecast / climatology p_wet) ┼→ Itinerary → Budget → Aggregator
                                            └ Transport (OSRM + cost table)          ┘
```

Itinerary has two modes (`PLANNER=llm|robust`). In `robust` mode it makes no LLM call: the LLM's only
influence is the ranked candidate pool, which enters the utility.

### 3.1 Model

For candidates *i* and days *d*: binary *x[i,d]* (visit), *r[i,d]* (indoor *i* reserved as day *d*'s
fallback) and *o[d]* (day *d* has an outdoor stop). Utility *u_i* is the Research agent's score
(interest match, notability, distance) plus a bonus for the LLM's rank. With wet-day probability
*p_d*, rain loss *ρ* and outdoor flag *out_i*:

```
max  Σ x[i,d]·u_i·(1 − ρ·p_d·out_i) + Σ ½·p_d·u_i·r[i,d] − M·(Σ s_cov + Σ s_wet)
s.t. Σ_d x[i,d] + Σ_d r[i,d] ≤ 1                       each place once
     Σ_i x[i,d] ≤ cap(pace)                            pace
     Σ_i (visit_i + minin_i)·x[i,d] ≤ window_d         relaxed time  (valid lower bound)
     Σ_i minin_i·x[i,d] ≤ drive_d                      relaxed drive (valid lower bound)
     o[d] ≥ x[i,d]  (outdoor i),  Σ_i r[i,d] ≥ o[d] − s_wet[d]   (p_d ≥ 0.5)   weather safety
     Σ_{i∈I_k,d} x[i,d] ≥ 1 − s_cov[k]                 interest coverage
     Σ_{i∈S} x[i,d] ≤ |S| − 1   for every infeasible core S found on day d     Benders no-good cuts
```

*minin_i* is the shortest leg into *i* from anywhere, so the relaxed time and drive rows never cut off
a feasible day. The **subproblem** orders a day's places exactly (enumeration up to 7 stops) and
simulates the timeline. If the day is infeasible, a deletion filter shrinks the set to a minimal
infeasible core, which becomes a cut. When no day needs a cut, the master's objective equals the
plan's, and the plan is optimal for the model.

### 3.2 Weather

Beyond the 16-day forecast horizon, *p_d* is the share of days within ±7 calendar days, over 10
years (5 in the live app), with ≥ 2.5 mm rain (IMD's "rainy day"). Inside the horizon it is Open-Meteo's
precipitation probability. The expected value of a day is
`(1 − p)·U(A) + p·max(U_wet(A), U(B))`, where *B* is an indoor fallback re-optimised from the day's
indoor stops, its reservation and unused places.

## 4. Experimental setup

- **Cases.** The 40 fixed requests in `eval/cases.jsonl` (North-East India, hill stations, metros,
  coast/pilgrimage; 1–5 days; 5 deliberately over-budget). Each is run in two regimes: its own dates
  (Nov–Dec) and the same trip shifted to July (monsoon).
- **Frozen inputs.** `research/snapshot.py` stores each case's candidate pool (Overpass → the
  production `pre_rank`), the OSRM travel-time matrix and a 10-year rainfall series. Every system
  plans from identical inputs.
- **Systems.** `greedy` (TravelMate's deterministic fallback), `llm_pipeline` (TravelMate before this
  work: the LLM groups IDs, then Python repairs), `llm_raw` (the LLM's grouping, optimally ordered,
  unrepaired), `llm_modulo` (llm_raw plus up to 3 critic back-prompts), `milp` (ours, weather-blind
  ablation) and `milp_robust` (ours, full). LLM: NVIDIA Nemotron Ultra, temperature 0, with
  retry on rate limits so outages are not scored as failures.
- **Metrics.** TravelPlanner's six rates over our 10 constraints, plan value (expected, dry, all-wet)
  as % of the best system on the same case, paired bootstrap 95% CIs, solver statistics.
- **Fairness.** All rows are re-scored by the final critic bank (`report.rescore`). Within Sandbox
  uses the planner's raw output from the original run.

## 5. Results

See `research/results/report.md` (Tables T1–T6) and the interactive demo built by
`python -m research.build_demo`. Headline numbers are summarised in the README.

## 6. Limitations

- Utility is a transparent score, not a learned preference model. The LLM's rank enters as a small
  bonus.
- The weather model is climatological and per-day. It ignores within-day timing and correlation
  between consecutive days. *ρ* is an assumption, swept in T5.
- Plans are scored against the model's own travel-time matrix. The live app re-routes with OSRM and
  trims if real legs are longer.
- Prices come from a preliminary cost table (docs/DATA_SOURCES.md). Budget is handled by the existing
  deterministic Budget agent and is not part of this comparison.

### Table A1. Constraint mapping from TravelPlanner

| TravelPlanner | TravelMate-R | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Within Sandbox | every stop ID came from the tools | commonsense |
| Within Current City | every stop is a day trip from the stay | commonsense |
| Diverse Attractions | no place repeated | commonsense |
| Complete Information | no empty day while an unused place fits it | commonsense |
| Non-conf. Transportation | Day Window: day ends inside its window (after arrival, before departure) | commonsense |
| (new) | Drive Limit: daily driving within the pace budget, intercity trip included | commonsense |
| (new) | Opening Hours: no visit outside listed hours | commonsense |
| Room Type / House Rule | Pace: stops per day within the pace limit | hard |
| Cuisine | Interest Coverage: every requested interest available nearby is covered | hard |
| (new) | Weather Safety: a likely-wet outdoor day has an indoor Plan B | hard |
